Purpose and exclusions

Inventory is a bounded collection of stack/instance records. UI drag/drop requests a move; the backend commits ownership and capacity changes. Slot index alone is not a safe identity for a mutable item.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create URPGInventoryComponent on PlayerState for owner-only in-zone inventory projection. Persistent rows remain in the backend.
  2. Create DA_Inventory_Default with 16 slots and explicit expansion rules; WBP_Inventory builds slots from capacity, not a fixed six-slot legacy panel.
  3. Add item-row/slot UMG widgets only as reusable presentational children; their OnDrop handlers call inventory requests, not SetArrayElem on the authoritative model.
  4. Seed Bag16 with one full ore stack, one partial stack, a sword instance and one final empty slot. Add a full-bag variation for capacity tests.
  5. Reopen loot, merchant, craft, gather and fishing owners to use the same authoritative capacity planner inside their transaction; do not each implement divergent stacking rules.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

ContractExecution / effect
RequestMove(CommandId, SourceContainer, SourceSlot, ExpectedItem, DestinationSlot, Quantity) -> Moved|StaleItem|NoSpaceNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
RequestSplitStack(CommandId, StackIdentity, Quantity, DestinationSlot) -> Split|InvalidQuantity|NoSpaceNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
PreviewCapacity(PlannedRewards) -> Fits|NoSpace; UI hint, repeated authoritativelyNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.
ApplyInventorySnapshot(Revision, Slots) -> Updated|Stale; owner-only observerNative current owner; local request versus server validation as the command states. Backend work is asynchronous, cosmetics observe only after accepted state.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Inventory bags, stacks, capacity and atomic moves. Rule owner: URPGInventoryComponent. This asset’s role is Inventory is a bounded collection of stack/instance records. UI drag/drop requests a move; the backend commits ownership and capacity changes. Slot index alone is not a safe identity for a mutable item.

  1. Player drags a stable item view or requests split quantity; UI sends expected identity/revision and destination, then marks involved slots pending.
  2. Server checks owned session, request bounds, allowed container types and action state; backend locks character/container rows and resolves the actual current source.
  3. Validate stack compatibility, available quantity, destination capacity and binding. Simulate all deltas before applying any.
  4. Commit source/destination changes, inventory revision and receipt together. For a swap validate both sides; never remove the source before discovering the destination cannot accept it.
  5. Zone updates owner-only replicated projection; WBP_Inventory reconciles by identity/revision and restores pending focus after result.
  6. After timeout/reconnect, query receipt and snapshot. Do not recreate dragged items or trust locally cached slot contents.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / Character_A / Bag16 / Slot15Occupied. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Two grants competing for final slot -> only a valid serial result commits; no overflow bag.
Split zero, negative or more than owned -> InvalidQuantity, unchanged inventory.
Move request uses old item UUID after swap -> StaleItem, never moves the replacement.
Disconnect during drag -> no mutation unless a command committed; reconnection shows durable result.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
